calls.reason: The packet has no 2019-to-2023 comparison. Magar and Schwartz found contamination is sometimes exploited and sometimes not, while OpenAI's own audit reported little effect on scores, so the evidence is mixed and indirect.

San Francisco's filing records Waymo cars interfering with emergency scenes, but Waymo's crash simulations and insurance-claims study point the other way. None of it measures unusual situations against matched human drivers.

The counterfactual-task study and the unpublished formal-system test drew conclusions about transfer without seeing training data, but neither could fully guarantee novelty. That leaves the strong 'almost impossible' claim unsettled.

Vectara's November 2023 leaderboard shows nonzero hallucination rates (3–27%), and Zhang et al. report high faithfulness in a news-summary setting. Nothing sets a reliability threshold, and nothing is dated to August 2023.
The DeepMind survey lists earlier AGI definitions built on typical-human tasks, which casts doubt on 'we all'. But it does not measure what the field believed in February 2022.
This is a stated opinion ('in my view'). The 2022 exchange was not recovered, and Legg's October 2023 interview only adds context, so the evidence can't show whether his standard changed.
